saw_lines: Men buying a suit online want to know it arrives before the wedding and that a wrong size can go back.
So the delivery answer belongs in the first line of the ad, because a buyer who cannot see it scrolls past.
Your site explains how it ships, yet 0 of 30 ads mention shipping or delivery. Answer the shipping question in the first line of ads for new buyers.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 15 Oct 2026
points: Your site offers free shipping in Europe, yet 0 of 30 ads mention shipping or delivery, so a new buyer has no reason to click. Open three new ads with the free shipping line, then the delivery time.
None of your 14 written ads carries a proof number, so a man comparing tailors has nothing firm to hold onto. Collect one figure you can stand behind, like a review count, and lead three ads with it.
16 of your 30 ads are catalog feed ads with no story, so a shopper sees a product with no reason to stop. Write three story ads, one on how a suit gets fitted, one on a brand you stock.
6 Shop now ads send buyers to the homepage, so a man who clicks has to hunt for the item again. Point each one at the exact product or collection in the creative, such as a Barbour jacket or a suit.
